test_title: SSC CPO 2022 Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.**

I asked Joe to meet for lunch on Saturday.

options.text: I says, “Let’s meet for lunch on Saturday Joe”.
I said, “Let’s meet for lunch on Saturday, Joe”.
I said, “We shall meet for lunch at Saturday Joe”.
I said, “Let’s meets for lunch at Saturday Joe”.

solution:
The correct answer:** "I said, 'Let's meet for lunch on Saturday, Joe'."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• The rules of changing Indirect to Direct speech for imperative sentence conversions.

 
 
• We must insert a comma before the name of the person being addressed.
 
• We must add quotation marks around the actual words spoken.
 
• We must use the reporting verb **"said"** instead of **"asked".**
 
• Change the tense of the reporting verb from past tense to present tense.
 
• The first person in the reported speech changes according to the subject of reporting speech.
 
• In Reported Speech change of the second person depends on the object of reporting speech.
 
• Imperative sentences do not normally have an expressed subject.
 
• This is because the subject** ‘you’** is usually understood.
 
• In order to change an imperative sentence into direct speech, we must remove a to-infinitive from direct speech.
 
 
• Example: 
 
• *The old woman said to the boy, ‘Let's watch the movie.’*
 
• *The old woman said the boy to watch the movie.*
 
 
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.

 

Correct sentence: *"I said, 'Let's meet for lunch on Saturday, Joe'."*
